The perf session's bf16 padding is a sandbox proposal for the Stu owner, with no path in this frozen FP32 runtime. Max09:17's fix for the failed Gen9/Azure4 cache-source restart is scoped to that job; no general collector transition is issued and this stream retains the user's explicit new-source/new-identity rule. No local source amendment, guard weakening, model/settings change, data import, training, external message or peer command.

Arena runtime: a run goes on after a harness change listed in its folder's source-amendments.json

Max, 14 Nov 09:17 UTC, after the Gen 9 cohort refused 7e0edac7 ("Pinned generation source changed"): "Fix it
so that it can run with changed code. Producing the boards is more important."

bridge_harness/mixed_arena.py: verify_generation's source check is check_source(). The pinned source passes as
before. A different source passes only if the run folder's source-amendments.json lists its sha256 with a
reason, and the accepting entry is printed to stderr. Anything else is refused, and the message names the
refused source's full hash, so the entry can be written from the log.

Unchanged: the manifest identity, the runtime files (ops/gen5_runtime.py, ops/prepare_gen7_alpha.py), the bot
identities and artifacts, and the corpus are all still checked. Records are still validated against the
manifest identity and the bots' versions.

This is feature/gen9-cohort-sync (7e0edac7, the cache's sync switch) plus this commit.
tests/test_source_amendments.py: 5 tests. tests/test_dds_cache_sync.py and tests/test_gen9_cohort.py pass.

bf16 nets: pad batches to fixed sizes (gen7_net.bucket) so oneDNN stops building kernels for every new size

With BRIDGE_NET_BF16=1 the rollouts' changing batch sizes made oneDNN build a kernel
for each new shape and grow its cache. Padding each bf16 call (Bf16Forward and the
FitScorer's bf16 layers) to about 25 fixed sizes and cutting the padding off: in the
sandbox (Sapphire Rapids) self-play goes from 26.0 to 13.9 CPU-s a board and a worker's
peak memory from 2.3 to 1.4 GB, the same cards on 6 boards, outputs bit-identical.
Not yet measured on the Zen 4 boxes. BRIDGE_NET_BUCKETS=0 turns it off.

training/perf-20261114: profile of a pure-Stu table and the bench scripts.

mailbridge: a mailbox for a Claude session, relayed by a box through an encrypted channel branch

mailbridge.py runs on the box (IMAP poll and SMTP send each minute, allow-listed
recipients); client.py runs in the session; branch mail/coord carries CMS
sign-then-encrypt blobs because the repository is public. Tested end to end with
tests/test_mailbridge.py against a local bare repository and a fake transport;
the Gmail transport is untested until the live box.
